orderRationale: Prioritize shared language contracts and the smallest linked application graph. The listed dependencies are semantic prerequisites, not a promise that all other tasks are serial.
measurement: Inventory includes uncalled bodies and direct syntax only; it is a conservative risk map, not a count of remaining failures, a coverage percentage or an ETA. Demand and isolated runtime checks refine it.

steps.work: Refresh linked-source prerequisites for all three pinned applications, including uncalled bodies and direct global/native API uses.
acceptanceAndRisks: No source is dropped when lowering refuses an earlier construct.
Keep locations and distinguish resolver sources from linked sources; syntax occurrences do not prove demand or unsupported semantics.
Audit aliases, reflective calls and conditional resolution separately.

steps.work: Resolve the MCP/Ajv runtime-generated validator path before claiming complete no-engine application support.

evidence.fact: Constructs new Function from generated sourceCode.
Defaults to new AjvJsonSchemaValidator when no custom validator is supplied.

acceptanceAndRisks: The static graph contains this code, including uncalled bodies; determine demanded calls and whether schemas are available at compilation or arrive at runtime.
Compile statically closed generated code through the AOT path only when its inputs and semantics are proven.
If runtime schemas demand the path, design a native Rust JSON-Schema validation contract and compare keywords/options, references, formats, errors and callable metadata with the pinned provider.
No JS engine, arbitrary source evaluator, ignored validation, removed branches, modified application/dependencies or compiler fallback.
No new Function/eval observation was found in the direct linked release inventory; keep the primary milestone separate from the larger application risk.

steps.work: Own primitive symbol identity across source types, containers, unions, erasure and exceptions.
acceptanceAndRisks: Symbol creation and registry identity match Node; equal descriptions never imply equality.
Keep well-known symbols, factory aliases, descriptor keys and unsupported coercions as explicit boundaries until covered.

steps.work: Represent console.log/error as first-class native callbacks, including aliases and dependency declaration signatures.
acceptanceAndRisks: Preserve function identity, argument evaluation, stdout/stderr selection and callback return type.
Exercise the red-dev log.ts shape; distinguish simple messages from format-string and object-inspection semantics.
steps.evidence: The native frontend now represents ambient log/info/debug/warn/error as stable portable closure values with one string argument, including aliases, scopes, captures, Node/DOM declaration variants and JS declaration contracts. rust-native-console has seven differential fixtures plus a standalone prelude integration; broader variadic/object formatting and alternate first-class signatures remain explicit boundaries.

steps.work: Represent TextEncoder/TextDecoder, byte buffers and the Web Streams contracts imported by the parser.
steps.evidence: Default nominal TextEncoder/TextDecoder allocation and typed UTF-8 encode/decode now use portable class/bytes IR and the shared Rust runtime; rust-native-codecs covers Unicode, BOM/replacement decoding, identity, views/copies, mutation, containers and evaluation order. The original release now passes both module initializers and refuses ToonlReader private fields at toonl.js:574. Streaming/options, ArrayBuffer and byte projections remain open.
acceptanceAndRisks: Preserve UTF-8/UTF-16 conversion, lone surrogates, decoder streaming/fatal/BOM modes and owning buffer aliasing.
Keep module-level codec allocation effects and identities; do not delete an initializer because its data path is unused.
Readable/Writable/TransformStream must preserve backpressure, cancellation, pipe/reader locking and error propagation before claiming stream support.
Native runtime functionality must be connected through owned types/IR; a declared browser/Node global is not a representation.

steps.work: Lower source loops, switch, updates and abrupt branch targets into owned structured IR.
acceptanceAndRisks: Preserve for initializer/test/update order, per-iteration lexical captures and var scope.
Break/continue/return/throw through nested finally must target the correct scope.
Test UTF-16 string indexing and live mutation separately from dense-array helper semantics.

steps.work: Add dependency destructuring, defaults, rest/spread and parameter binding without losing callable identities.
acceptanceAndRisks: Evaluate sources and computed keys once, in source order; apply defaults only for undefined.
Preserve holes, argument arity, own enumerable property ordering, accessors and symbol keys.
Keep function identity and module live bindings through aliases and destructuring.

For the gh Provider case preserve an absent bin property versus a present undefined value, evaluate the condition once, and retain spread/property precedence and observable own-key order. Do not rewrite optional spreads to unconditional undefined fields.
steps.evidence: Inline data-literal and conditional spreads use retained seqExpr/if/recordSet operations, including contextual Provider unions and public JS contracts. Six rust-native-spreads fixtures cover order, skipped branches, exceptions, aliases, keys and omission versus undefined. Typed array rest uses the retained rest:true/restAbi:array function type and fresh call-site packing, including aliases, captured/returned callbacks, public JS contracts, erased calls, nullable callee snapshots and bind of a fixed prefix. Six rust-native-array-rest fixtures cover these contracts against Node and both Rust backends. Closed typed record sources now supply required fields through a private construction plan with a definite-write proof and ordered key/value snapshots. record.cloneOwn materializes a fresh, complete record without exposing partial typed storage. Six rust-native-record-build programs compare copying, order, own-key presence, callback/array/record identity, exceptions and public JS contracts with Node and both Rust backends. Original application retries are recorded with the checkpoint evidence; a later diagnostic is not an application acceptance milestone. Generic source rest, instance/constructor rest, tuple-rest source binding, iterable call spreads, fixed builtin callback adaptation and binding rest elements retain explicit boundaries. Leading record-union spreads now distribute by owned IR tags with one lossless target layout per source arm, evaluating the source once and only the selected trailing initializers. Six rust-native-union-spreads programs cover provider flags, same-typed member reads, collapsed literal domains, order, exceptions, identity, own-key presence and public JS contracts against Node and both Rust backends. Prefix/multiple-source correlation, field-type changes and ambiguous projections remain explicit boundaries. Named data records now share an owning Rust property store behind typed IR views. record.view maps invariant source/target arms without allocation or property loss; record.setOwn and record.fromOwn preserve every own property through later spreads, including keys hidden by static views. Six rust-native-record-views programs cover provider coercions, typed/erased alias writes, callbacks/arrays, cycles, key presence/order, prototype data keys, union tags, snapshots, exceptions and JS contracts against Node and both Rust backends. Field-type-changing, ambiguous and nullable source views remain boundaries.

nativeParameterDefaultContract.implementation: Lower the initializer once against the complete incoming native type. Keep undefined in the separate mutable body binding when the lowered default can still produce it. Project proven defined defaults without repeating initializer effects. Presence tests, assignments, captures and var redeclarations retain the native fact even when declaration files promise a narrower value.
coverage: Omitted and explicit undefined; null and false/zero supplied values; optional records, arrays and functions.
Earlier-parameter references, initializer/argument order, conditional defaults and thrown defaults.
Mutable captures, function aliases, closures, constructors, methods and an eager async prefix.
Native process stream isTTY defaults and body var redeclarations; pipe execution plus a supplemental real-PTY stdin comparison.
boundaries: Standalone unit-only parameter storage and parameter TDZ access remain explicit refusals.
This keeps the existing caller ABI and portable IR; it does not add await suspension or direct async Promise return adoption.

steps.work: Broaden dependency object APIs, class private fields/accessors/static members, native callable receivers, unions and recursive handle layouts.
acceptanceAndRisks: Cover Object.keys/entries/assign/fromEntries, descriptors/prototypes and symbol-keyed storage as separate contracts.
Do not project nominal classes into structural records or invent an ABI for incompatible overrides.
Preserve absence versus undefined, GC ownership and object/function identity across public JS signatures.
Private instance slots need declaration-owned names and receiver brands; never expose #name as a public string key or conflate equal spelling in different classes.
Getter/setter reads and writes must evaluate the receiver once and invoke the correct accessor, including inheritance, super and exceptions.
Keep definition-time effects distinct from construction-time field initializers and demanded method/accessor bodies; deferring a body does not authorize deleting an executable initializer.
steps.evidence: The original release boundary after module-level codec allocation is ToonlReader #source/#cursor/#state and get cursor in @reddb-io/toon/dist/toonl.js:573 onward; preserve private brands and accessor invocation rather than deleting the class declaration. After file-backed metadata support, red-dev reaches Signal.get value/set value in tuiuiu.js/dist/primitives/signal.js. Reads may track the active Effect; writes compare with Object.is before notifying subscribers. Both need the same owned class/accessor model, with explicit boundaries for unported dependent calls.

nativeSetMilestone.implementation: Owned scalar, record, function, symbol and dynamic element layouts. Heterogeneous element unions use tagged native membership storage. Native and reference Rust comparisons preserve SameValueZero and normalized positive-zero storage. Existing Set IR and shared Rust runtime are retained.
boundaries: General iterable seeds, dynamic/function nonliteral seeds, unsupported typed element layouts and Set erasure.
Frontend values()/next()/spread iteration and live mutation during iteration remain separate contracts.
nativeSetMilestone.evidence: Six new harmless programs match Node 24.15 through the Rust frontend and both Rust emitters. New reference API tests observe NaN collapse, stored positive zero and delete/reinsert order. The prior record-seed refusal is now a positive differential case; artifact-preserving iteration refusal remains tested. Original red-dev passes the registeredScopes Set and hook-warning Set initializers.

nativeWeakMapMilestone.trigger: red-dev node_modules/tuiuiu.js/dist/hooks/context.js:864..878 constructs appRuntimeScopes = new WeakMap(). Source uses get(appContext), set(ctx, resolvedScope) and delete(previous).
nativeWeakMapMilestone.implementation: Default nominal owning identities lower get/set/has/delete through validated weakmap.* operations in IR v13. Closed data-record keys retain identity through typed views. Owning values use conditional registry edges: collector reference-count accounting excludes those edges from outside roots, then fixed-point marking activates them only when both map owner and key are live. Inactive entries are removed before garbage edges are cleared.
boundaries: Constructor iterables, extracted methods, subclasses and WeakMap erasure/reflection remain refused.
Other key representations, including arrays, functions, class instances and symbols, remain explicit boundaries; the record-key subset does not imply general weak-key support.
WeakSet, finalization callbacks and source-visible GC APIs require separate contracts.
nativeWeakMapMilestone.evidence: Six harmless programs compare identity, typed record views, overwrites, stored undefined, argument/error order, owning values, queued/captured cycles, module storage and source shadows with Node 24.15 through both Rust emitters. Six deterministic runtime tests prove dead key/owner cleanup, conditional chain activation, mutually dependent keys and scalar-only entry pruning. Artifact-preserving boundary tests keep unsupported forms explicit; reference API assertions validate serialized signatures and C/LLVM refusal. The original red-dev now passes the WeakMap initializer and refuses url.fileURLToPath in core/dev-warnings.js.
acceptanceAndRisks: Retain per-instance identity and object-key identity through get/set/has/delete, aliases and declaration/runtime boundaries; preserve absent versus stored undefined and chaining.

Keys must not become ordinary strong roots. Values may refer back to keys through runtime scopes and hook state; account for ephemeron reachability rather than replacing WeakMap with Map or relying only on Rc weak keys while strongly rooting every value.

Integrate conditional edges and dead-entry cleanup with the native heap collector and prove owning cycles/finish cleanup. Run harmless object-key differential programs and deterministic collector-level tests.

Validate receiver/key failures and preserve source evaluation order. Other weak-key domains, constructor iterables, extracted methods, reflection and WeakSet need their own evidence or explicit refusal.
No empty-object placeholder, JS engine, source evaluator, compiler fallback or edits to original applications/dependencies.

steps.work: Compile synchronous iterators and source generators, especially the streaming parser dependency.
acceptanceAndRisks: Keep suspended local state, generator identity, next/return/throw and delegated yields.
IteratorClose and generator finally run exactly when Node runs them; never eagerly consume a lazy generator.
Test the original parser in isolated encode/decode scenarios before claiming the dependency works.

steps.work: Compile async functions, await and async iteration with pending completions across suspension.
acceptanceAndRisks: Preserve microtask order, rejected awaits, adoption, thenables and return/throw replacement by finally.
Include rejection handlers, Promise.all heterogeneous results, top-level await and entry completion.
Async iteration must close on abrupt exits and preserve cleanup failures.

observedNativeMilestone.entryDemand: The native reachability report traces the function from a call at agents.ts:41322..41385; body compilation does not execute the original probe.
contracts: Keep call signatures returning Promise<T> separate from async function body return type T in owned IR and native validation.

Run the prefix at call time; suspend await continuations on the job queue with owning traced cells and preserve pending return/throw/finally through try/catch. Do not implement await by blocking until completion.

Port the demanded Bun.spawn argv/options contract and stdout stream ownership to native Rust subprocess/stream APIs. Response.text() must drain through the async stream contract and proc.exited must settle independently with correct errors/status.

Keep the source-runtime Bun contract explicit and compare harmless child-process fixtures with its pinned oracle; Node remains the independent oracle for shared language behavior. No Bun/Node/TS/Go production fallback and no original provisioning/release execution.

nativeUnsuspendedContract.implementation: Portable async function flag; body T versus callable Promise<T>; eager defaults/body, exception-to-rejection conversion, protected completions and queued fulfillment/rejection reactions. Named declarations, anonymous closures and source methods share the ABI.
remaining: Await continuations and traced suspension frames
Direct async Promise return adoption after finalizers
Async iteration and top-level entry completion
Bun subprocess/stream API adapter and pinned harmless oracle
nativeUnsuspendedContract.returnAdoptionBoundary: Direct Promise returns remain unsupported even without await, including erased Promise<unknown> contracts. A harmless audit built successfully but reached the existing native erased promise.then runtime boundary when resolving its return; Node fulfilled with a number. Treat this as refusal evidence, not successful support, and include it in adoption acceptance.

nativeAsyncContextMilestone.trigger: red-dev node_modules/tuiuiu.js/dist/core/runtime-scope.js:782..806 constructs new AsyncLocalStorage() at module initialization.
nativeAsyncContextMilestone.runtimeAvailable: The Rust frontend, native IR validator and emitter now connect nominal AsyncLocalStorage instances to the existing shared Rust runtime through portable IR v13 als.new/get/run operations. The runtime itself is unchanged.
acceptance: Keep independent store identity and the real store value, including stored undefined versus an absent context where observable; do not substitute one mutable global scope.
Restore nested run/exit scopes after normal returns and throws, evaluate receiver/store/callback/arguments in source order and preserve callback return identity.
Capture context at reaction/job registration and prove isolation across interleaved promise chains, with Node differential fixtures.
Trace owning store values and queued context captures; exercise record/function cycles and finish cleanup rather than relying only on existing scalar runtime tests.
Connect the existing native runtime contract without an engine or compiler fallback; unsupported options, bind/snapshot and broader async_hooks APIs remain explicit boundaries until implemented.
nativeAsyncContextMilestone.implementation: Default constructor, run(value, callback, ...fixedArguments), getStore(), independent owning identity, caller-side argument snapshots, RAII restoration after normal/exceptional returns and promise-reaction registration contexts. Never-returning callbacks preserve abrupt completion through a unit ABI.
boundaries: Constructor options, enterWith/exit/disable, bind/snapshot and broader async_hooks APIs.
Extracted methods, subclasses, instance erasure/reflection, including erasure through containers and function return types.
General suspension and Promise return adoption retain their separate milestones.
nativeAsyncContextMilestone.evidence: Seven harmless programs match Node 24.15 through the native Rust compiler and reference Rust backend, including interleaved contexts, throws, callback argument effects, records/functions/Promises and queued owning cycles. Boundary integration preserves preexisting artifacts. The original red-dev compile now passes the AsyncLocalStorage initializer and refuses registeredScopes = new Set() at runtime-scope.js:832..842.

steps.work: Support reachable dynamic imports/CommonJS patterns, import.meta and Node entry/process contracts.
acceptanceAndRisks: Respect conditional package exports, module cache identity, cycles, top-level effects and dynamic-import completion.
Match argv/env/platform/cwd/exitCode/stdout/stderr and entry guards; do not skip dependency initialization.
No runtime source evaluation, TS/Go fallback or replacement application entry.

fileModuleMetadataMilestone.implementation: Direct file-backed import.meta.url/filename/dirname reads lower to owned strings from the canonical defining source module, including imported functions and captures. Default-platform one-string fileURLToPath calls reuse url.fileURLToPathStr in IR v13 and the shared Rust runtime. Strict decoding preserves URI errors, error codes, separator precedence, Windows encoded drive letters and Unicode UNC hosts.
boundaries: Whole/escaped metadata objects, indexed/destructured reads, mutation and import.meta.resolve/main remain refused.
URL-object input and explicit fileURLToPath options remain frontend boundaries; runtime string decoding support does not imply those overloads.
fileModuleMetadataMilestone.evidence: Native and reference Rust differential programs compare canonical module provenance, imported calls, parameter ABI, captures, Unicode/percent paths, validation order and failures against Node 24.15. A native integration compares an unusual source filename from a different working directory. Original red-dev passes dev-warnings.js module path initialization and next refuses the Signal value getter.

namespaceMilestone.trigger: red-dev manifest.ts:1512 stores typeof import("./machine-profile.ts") | null; the next function uses lazy require with ??=.
namespaceMilestone.investigation: A harmless two-export namespace stored through an alias reproduces an unlowered namespace value independently of the application. The real red-dev package has type:module and dev/build scripts using Bun. Import namespace identity and source-runtime require semantics need separate contracts.
acceptance: Owning canonical namespace identity in locals, module storage, aliases and nullable containers; do not eagerly lower every exported generic signature just to store a namespace handle.
Read demanded exports through the module binding table and preserve live values, TDZ, reexports and cycles; do not copy mutable exports into ordinary data fields.
Keep namespace mutation, dynamic keys, own-key order and toStringTag either correctly represented or explicitly refused.
Preserve the default Node ambient-require refusal for ESM; Bun source-runtime behavior requires an explicit adapter/profile and isolated oracle evidence, never a production Bun fallback.
Lazy requests initialize once at the original call site, preserving errors, partially initialized cycles and synchronous/asynchronous module boundaries.
namespaceMilestone.evidence: Four rust-native-namespaces programs cover nullable caches, aliases and typed containers/callbacks, current mutable exports, reexports, receiver/argument order, callee snapshots, cycles and read/write TDZ. Module handles lower to private empty owning capsules; values are read from the module binding table after receiver evaluation. In the reference Rust backend, explicit initializesGlobal markers track lexical readiness separately from physical scalar/heap slots, including suspended assignments. Old unmarked producers retain their previous storage contract. Namespace descriptors and lazy ESM require are not implied.

nativeLexicalInitializers.implementation: Initialize uninitialized lexical identifiers with undefined at their declaration site through existing owning slots and initializesGlobal markers. Preserve module read/write TDZ, RHS effects, cyclic imports, captures and optional containers. Untyped JS declarations without an initializer use native owning Dyn storage.
boundaries: Ambient lexical declarations have no native runtime binding.
Storage without an undefined representation is refused; definite-assignment assertions never authorize an invented zero.

nativeJavaScriptUnitStorage.implementation: Unannotated JS lexical declarations with null/undefined initializers reserve owning native value storage when the checker supplies an erased or unit-only type. Initialization remains at the source site through existing initialization markers; subsequent writes keep tags, identities and traced captures. Public JS declaration contracts continue to select typed call and return ABIs.
coverage: Null, undefined, string, boolean and numeric transitions, falsy values, constant units and a shadowed undefined identifier.
Records, arrays, functions, snapshots, independent captured cells and an owning cycle under heap audit.
Read/write TDZ, RHS-before-write effects and live module bindings through import cycles.
Typed .d.ts return and parameter contracts over a JS dependency with a private null/string cache.
boundaries: TypeScript unit-only storage and source unit-only function returns retain their existing refusals.
No changes to the shared runtime, IR version or caller ABI.

steps.work: Expose the native runtime APIs and options used by the linked release dependency graph.
acceptanceAndRisks: Prioritize fs sync/promises with options, directory entries and errors; then subprocess status/signal/stdin/stdout/stderr.
Cover JSON/Date/URL/Buffer/crypto and GitHub HTTP/stream response shapes from source evidence.
Use temporary directories, injected fixtures and local services for comparisons; do not run real releases or provisioning.

steps.work: Implement the Bun APIs used by the original applications as native Rust operations over the owned ABI.
steps.evidence: Original red-dev sources use Bun.spawn/spawnSync, Bun.which, Bun.file(...).text(), Bun.write, Bun.TOML.parse and Bun shell tagged templates. Static linked-source counts are recorded separately from source-text checks.
acceptanceAndRisks: No Bun executable, JS engine, source evaluator or compiler fallback in the resulting application.
Preserve subprocess pipes/status/signals, file handles/Response bytes and TOML/shell error and quoting contracts.
Use Node parity for Node-compatible programs; Bun-only source behavior needs a separately pinned Bun oracle, never an invented Node parity claim through shims.
Do not replace the original entry or dependencies to make a build pass.

steps.work: Separate compiler correctness, reference interoperability and toolchain/host failures before shipping.
acceptanceAndRisks: Keep native Node differential and IR/reference matrices enabled on Windows and Ubuntu.
Preserve the protected Rust corpus and heap audits; include wrong-type, failure and artifact-atomicity tests.
Resolve the existing LLVM multi-instance SAN failure and obtain a completed plain run; a 240-second timeout is not a pass.
Investigate Defender reference-executable rejection without exclusions or disabled protection.

steps.work: Emit the original pinned release binary and compare isolated application behavior, then expand to redskilled and red-dev.
acceptanceAndRisks: All original entries and dependency snapshots remain unchanged.
Check isolated --help/version/error exits and parser/filesystem scenarios against Node.
Verify no engine or fallback is linked; shipping requires the repository gates.
A later first diagnostic does not satisfy this milestone.

conditionalDependencies.when: The original linked entry/dependencies require Bun-specific runtime APIs.
Demand reaches runtime-generated JavaScript validators or other source constructors.

steps.work: Distribute the validated Rust driver as the default compiler and retire compatibility pieces only after their callers and replacement contracts are covered.
acceptanceAndRisks: Match project configuration, package resolution, diagnostics, artifact modes, cache identity and supported library/CLI interfaces.
Production source checking/lowering/emission must remain Rust with no automatic legacy retry.
Preserve the reference oracle until its replacement and independent interoperability checks exist; reconcile pending legacy edits deliberately.

unknownsToAudit: Aliased/reflective global and Node API calls; inspector currently records direct syntax.
Declaration/implementation overload mismatches and erased callable receiver contracts.
Platform/environment-specific package branches, native addons, eval/Function constructors and dynamic require paths.
Data-dependent generic/recursive layouts, hidden prototype effects and implicit coercion.
Application behavior after a successful build: emitted code alone does not establish Node parity.
Other source operators, optional chains, remaining rest binding forms and implicit coercion paths need semantic demand checks beyond the current structural syntax categories.
GlobalThis/member aliases and builtin values used as callbacks are only partially visible to direct global-syntax inventory.
runtimeOraclePolicy: Native corpus remains differential against the pinned Node. Original applications and dependency behaviors must be compared against their actual source runtime; Bun-only contracts require explicit separate oracle evidence. Oracles are test tools and are never production fallbacks.

observedFirstRefusals.red-dev: node_modules/tuiuiu.js/dist/primitives/signal.js:712..910 Signal value getter. Getter dependency tracking and setter notification must preserve receiver identity and side effects; dev-warnings.js fileURLToPath/import.meta module initialization has been passed.
observedFirstRefusals.nextClassConstraint: Prioritize a shared private-slot and public-accessor model for ToonlReader and Signal. Keep declaration-owned private brands, receiver identity, inherited accessors, argument/RHS order, getter tracking and setter notifications. Object.is, Set iteration and the parser's computed async generator remain separate demanded dependencies; passing class registration alone does not establish application behavior.
observedFirstRefusals.nextCoercionConstraint: Keep the native undefined fact established by default lowering across body var redeclarations and captures; do not replace it with the checker declaration-file narrowing.
observedFirstRefusals.nextModuleConstraint: Keep canonical defining-module provenance for file-backed metadata and retain declaration-site initialization/module TDZ. Metadata reflection/mutation, import.meta.main/resolve, additional URL overloads, async suspension, direct Promise return adoption, Bun subprocess/Response streams, native namespace descriptors and async iteration remain outstanding.
observedFirstRefusals.nextStorageConstraint: Keep null/undefined JS lexical initialization separate from the permanent storage representation and from public typed call/return contracts. Preserve declaration-site initialization, captures and module TDZ.
observedFirstRefusals.nextAsyncContextConstraint: Keep the implemented run/getStore subset explicit; additional methods need their own context propagation and error contracts, especially disable across previously captured contexts.
observedFirstRefusals.nextCollectionConstraint: Keep conditional WeakMap reachability and dead-entry cleanup for record keys, including value-to-key and value-to-owner cycles. Other weak-key domains and iterable constructors remain explicit boundaries. Native Set iteration/values().next() is a separate outstanding contract.
